chunks: As for what Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from 'Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Suwayd al-Qalla', from Abi Ayyub, from Abi Basir, who said:

I asked him about a man who forgets and thus prays four rak'ahs while traveling. He said: If he remembers on that very day, then let him repeat it; and if he does not remember until that day passes, then there is no repetition upon him.

So what this report contains of the command to repeat after the expiration of the time within that day is to be understood as a form of recommendation. And what the first report contains of making it up so long as one remains within the time is upon obligation and requirement, and there is no contradiction between them in any way.

key_terms.أَرْبَعَ رَكَعَاتٍ: four units of prayer performed in full
key_terms.فِي السَّفَرِ: while in travel, meaning the state in which qasr prayer applies
key_terms.لَا إِعَادَةَ عَلَيْهِ: there is no required repetition upon him

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a traveler forgetfully prays four rak'ahs and remembers later?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling for a traveler who forgetfully performs a four-rak'ah salat instead of the shortened prayer. If he remembers within the same day, he should repeat it, while after the day has passed there is no obligatory repetition; the later discussion reconciles the reports by treating repetition after the prayer time as recommended rather than obligatory.
